attempts.text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"Thirty years of neoliberal Democratic and “free-market” Republican administrations have destroyed the publicly accountable federal regulation of capital and financial markets that social movements imposed during the Great Depression.", "claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Duplicitous accounting practices, corporate stripping of pension fund assets, predatory lending, and “mega-bank” marketing of nontransparent, speculative financial instruments have brought the productive economy to its knees.", "claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Democratic, public control of the financial system must be reasserted, rebuilt, and improved to rein in global capital’s scavenging for short-term speculative gain.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Restoring the 1938 Glass-Steagall Act’s separation of finance banks from commercial banks is necessary.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"Vigorous federal and state regulation of financial “rating agencies” is necessary so highly risky, speculative financial instruments are no longer certified as “investment grade” and “credit worthy”.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[5]},{"claim_text":"Re-creating a federally regulated savings and loan industry whose sole purpose is to provide affordable mortgages to middle- and working-class home buyers is necessary.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[6]},{"claim_text":"Strengthening federal and state support for worker- and consumer-owned credit unions that provide affordable credit to working- and middle-class consumers is necessary.", "claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[7]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
